title: Alistair Overeem teases shock return: 'I feel younger now than I did 5 years ago' - NewsBreak
text:
By Jordan Ellis ,
1 hours ago
Alistair Overeem poses on the scales ahead of a UFC Fight Night event in Phoenix in 2014, inset exclusive banner. Credit: Josh Hedges/Zuffa LLC/Zuffa LLC via Getty Images Alistair Overeem won’t rule out making a sensational comeback at 46 years old.
‘The Demolition Man’ hasn’t fought in MMA since being TKO’d by Alexander Volkov at UFC Vegas 18 in February 2021.
Since then, Alistair Overeem has competed in kickboxing against his long-time rival, Badr Hari.
The one-time UFC heavyweight title challenger won their October 2022 trilogy fight by unanimous decision, but the result was subsequently overturned to a no-contest due to a failed drug test .
EXCLUSIVE: Alistair Overeem expects Conor McGregor to retire after ‘rough night’ at UFC 329 Alistair Overeem has overcome the injury that retired him Alistair Overeem is feeling better than he did while competing after four years in retirement.
The former Strikeforce and Dream heavyweight champion continues to regularly train.
Overeem looks like he could fight again tomorrow, but does he feel like that is a possibility?
“An injury took me out of the sport,” Overeem said during an exclusive interview with Bloody Elbow.
“A lower back injury, it was nagging. It came back a couple of times in my career. The last time it didn’t want to go away, and it forced me out of the sport.
“I feel better now than I did five years ago. I feel younger. That being said, the time away did somewhat take me out of shape. I lost some mass.
“So, I’m just training, and I’m enjoying it. This is my bread and butter. It gives me pleasure. I’m just doing what I love. If it results in, ‘Hey, we feel like are going to kick ass again,’ which could be, you’ll be the first to know.”
